rows.note: Use this for the unexpectedly or surprisingly part of “curiously,” especially before an unexpected event or fact.

example.english: They ate the whole plate of food by themselves, curiously enough.
example.traditional: 佢竟然一個人食晒成盤嘢
example.jyutping: keoi5 ging2 jin4 jat1 go3 jan4 sik6 saai3 seng4 pun4 je5

rows.note: Use this when someone does something in a strange or odd manner rather than merely unexpectedly.

example.english: They smiled at their phone in a curiously odd way today.
example.traditional: 佢今日奇怪咁對住部電話笑
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam1 jat6 kei4 gwaai3 gam2 deoi3 zyu6 bou6 din6 waa2 siu3

rows.note: Use this colloquial framing when the speaker means that the result was not anticipated.

example.english: They won in the end, curiously enough.
example.jyutping: gu2 m4 dou2 keoi5 zan1 hai6 jeng4 zo2

rows.note: Use this sentence-initial phrase for “oddly, the curious thing is that …” when commenting on a strange fact.

example.english: People were still queuing outside the shop so late, curiously enough.
example.traditional: 奇怪嘅係，咁夜仲有人喺間舖出面排隊
example.jyutping: kei4 gwaai3 ge3 hai6 gam3 je6 zung6 jau5 jan4 hai2 gaan1 pou3 ceot1 min6 paai4 deoi6
